summary: House remains central to DJ sales, while Afro house, UK garage and faster club sounds show momentum across different measures. These sources describe different audiences and periods; they are not one combined genre ranking.
coverage: Beatport: January–June 2026; UK summer 2026 social/chart reporting; Splice/MIDiA: 2025 sample activity reported in Sounds of 2026. This is a reviewed snapshot, not live chart positions.

cards.evidence: Beatport’s midyear review keeps house and tech house at the centre of its 2026 sales picture. This measures one DJ marketplace, not all listening.
cards.productionTip: Keep the kick and bass distinct, and build a groove that works before adding more layers.

cards.evidence: Splice reports 778% year-on-year download growth for Afro house in 2025. MIDiA identifies it as a major contributor to house growth; sample demand is not streaming market share.
cards.productionTip: Give percussion room and let a restrained bassline support the rhythmic movement.

cards.evidence: Beatportal’s September report highlights UK garage and house in TikTok’s UK summer ranking. Splice separately reports speed-garage growth in 2025, supporting interest across two different measures.
cards.productionTip: Preserve shuffle and short bass phrases; leave gaps around vocal hooks.

cards.evidence: Beatport’s midyear report highlights melodic house and techno, while MIDiA reports growth in melodic-house sample activity. The sources describe different parts of the music market.
cards.productionTip: Let the main melody breathe and preserve contrast between the breakdown and drop.

cards.evidence: Beatport’s 2026 midyear review highlights Latin electronic and Brazilian funk among active club sounds. That supports exploration, rather than an inferred global ranking.
cards.productionTip: Build around a clear percussion identity and a memorable, concise vocal idea.

cards.evidence: MIDiA reports triple-digit 2025 sample-growth figures across hard techno, jump-up drum and bass, and hard dance. Beatport’s midyear report also discusses faster club styles.
cards.productionTip: Preserve drum attack and check harshness before pushing the final loudness.
